h: The expressions of the seventh day unveil different dimensions of Shabbat and humanity’s role in completing creation.
Three References to the Seventh Day

p: בְּפָרָשַׁת "וַיְכֻלּוּ" יֵשׁ ג׳ פְּעָמִים
In the passage of Vayechulu there are three occurrences of the phrase "
בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי".
'on the seventh day.'
וּבַגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת פח.) דִּקְדְּקוּ
And in the Gemara (Shabbat 88a) they scrutinized
עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "יוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי":
concerning that which is stated 'the sixth day' (Genesis 1:31):
הֵ״א יְתֵירָה לָמָּה לִי?
Why do I need the superfluous letter Hei?
וּדְרָשׁ לָהּ עַל שִׁשִּׁי בְּסִיוָון הַיָּדוּעַ,
And the Gemara expounded it as referring to the renowned sixth day of Sivan,
אִם מְקַבְּלִין יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה.
dependent on whether Israel accepts the Torah.
וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין
And one must understand:
הָנֵי ג׳ הֵהִי״ן יְתֵירִים דְּ"הַשְּׁבִיעִי",
these three superfluous letters Hei in the word HaShevi'i ('the seventh'),
מַאי דָּרְשֵׁי בְּהוּ?
what do the Sages expound concerning them?
אַךְ זֶה נִדְרַשׁ גַּם כֵּן לִדְרָשָׁא זוֹ:
However, this is likewise expounded according to this very exposition: "
אִם מְקַבְּלִין יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי",
'If Israel accepts the Torah, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ הַשְּׁבִיעִי הַיָּדוּעַ,
namely the renowned Seventh Day,
שֶׁהוּא שַׁבָּת שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה,
which is the Sabbath on which Israel received the Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שָׁם פו:):
as written (there, Shabbat 86b): "
וְדִכְלֵי עָלְמָא, בְּשַׁבָּת נִתְּנָה תוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל".
'And everyone agrees that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat.'
וּמִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל נִכְתַּב "הַשִּׁשִּׁי" הַיָּדוּעַ
– And from the perspective of Israel was written the renowned 'sixth'—
שִׁשִּׁי בְּסִיוָון,
the sixth of Sivan,
לְחֶשְׁבּוֹן הַחֹדֶשׁ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי לֵיהּ;
according to the reckoning of the lunar month which Israel sanctifies;
וּמִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִכְתַּב "הַשְּׁבִיעִי" הַיָּדוּעַ
whereas from the perspective of Hashem, blessed be He, was written the renowned 'seventh'
עַל שַׁבַּת דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
alluding to the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah,
שֶׁקְּדוּשַׁת הַשַּׁבָּת אֵינוֹ תָּלוּי בִּקְבִיעוּת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for the sanctity of the Sabbath is not dependent upon the calendar established by Israel,
רַק קְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא.
rather it is inherently fixed and immutable.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 88a: ‘Reish Lakish said: What is the meaning of that which is written, “And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day (yom ha-shishi)” (Genesis 1:31)? h: Rest as the Completion of Creation

p: וּכְתִיב: "וַיְכַל אֱלֹהִים בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי",
And it is written: 'And God finished on the seventh day' (Genesis 2:2),
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה י, ט):
in accordance with what is written in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 10:9): "
בָּאַת שַׁבָּת – בָּאַת מְנוּחָה",
'Shabbat arrived—rest arrived,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז הָיָה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִיּוּחָא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ,
meaning that then Hashem, blessed be He, experienced divine pleasure and serene satisfaction in His universe,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט, ד):
and as written (Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 9:4): "
עוֹלָמִי עוֹלָמִי, הַלְוַאי תְּהֵא מַעֲלַת חֵן לְפָנַי בְּכָל עֵת כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהֶעֱלֵיתָ חֵן לְפָנַי בְּשָׁעָה זוֹ".
'My world, My world! Would that you find favor before Me at all times just as you have found favor before Me at this hour!'
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וַיְכַל",
And this is why Scripture states Vayechal,
וּמְתַרְגֵּם בְּתַרְגּוּם יְרוּשַׁלְמִי: "וַחֲמִיד",
which the Targum Yerushalmi translates as: 'and He yearned/cherished,'
וּבַאֲבוּדַרְהָם שֶׁעַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת "חֶמְדַּת הַיָּמִים".
and cited in the Abudarham that on this account Shabbat is designated 'the coveted of days.'
וְעַל זֶה כְּתִיב "בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי",
And regarding this it is written 'on the seventh day',
שֶׁהַנִּיּוּחָא הָיָה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
for the divine satisfaction of Hashem, blessed be He, was
עַל מַה שֶּׁיְּקַבְּלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה בְּשַׁבָּת.
over the future reality that Israel would receive the Torah on Shabbat. "
וַיִּשְׁבֹּת בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ"
– 'And He rested on the seventh day from all His work'— "
וַיִּשְׁבֹּת" גַּם כֵּן לְשׁוֹן נִיּוּחָא וּמְנוּחָה.
Vayishbot is likewise an expression of tranquility and rest. "
מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ"
– 'From all His work'— "
כֹּל" מוֹרֶה עַל כָּל הֵיפֶךְ הַטּוֹב,
the word kol ('all') denotes every phenomenon opposite to the good,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה שָׁם פָּרָשָׁה ט)
just as expounded (Bereishit Rabbah there, parashah 9)
עַל "אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד"
– on the verse 'all that He had made, and behold, it was very good' (Genesis 1:31)—
עַל כָּל הֵיפֶךְ הַטּוֹב שֶׁגַּם כֵּן יִהְיֶה "טוֹב מְאֹד",
as applying to every opposite of good, that it too shall become 'very good',
כְּמוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע וְכַדּוֹמֶה.
such as the evil inclination and its like.
וְכֵן כְּתִיב: "וּבוֹרֵא רָע",
And so it is written (Isaiah 45:7): 'and creates evil,'
וְקָרֵינַן: "הַכֹּל", לִישְׁנָא מְעַלְּיָא (בְּרָכוֹת יא:),
yet we recite in the liturgy: 'Who forms all,' using a euphemistic phrasing (Berakhot 11b),
דְּ"הַכֹּל" מוֹרֶה עַל הַהֵיפֶךְ.
for the term 'all' encompasses the opposite.
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיְּקַבְּלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי.
And this transformation likewise occurs through Israel accepting the Torah on the seventh day. "
וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי"
– 'And God blessed the seventh day'—
לְשׁוֹן בְּרָכָה מוֹרֶה עַל רִיבּוּי,
the term 'blessing' denotes multiplication and expansion,
כְּמוֹ בְּרָכָה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה:
like the primary blessings in the Torah:
בְּרָכָה דִּדְגִים וּבְרָכָה דְּאָדָם.
the blessing over fish and the blessing over man.
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר אוֹר הַחַיִּים (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, ב),
And this aligns with what is written in the holy Ohr HaChayim (Genesis 2:2),
כִּי לֹא בָרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כֹּחַ בָּעוֹלָם זוּלַת לַעֲמוֹד שִׁשָּׁה יָמִים,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, imbued into the world vitality sufficient only to endure for six days,
וּבָרָא יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת,
and He created the Sabbath day,
וּבוֹ חוֹזֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמַשְׁפִּיעַ נֶפֶשׁ לָעוֹלָם
and upon it Hashem, blessed be He, returns and infuses a soul-vitality into the cosmos
הַמְקַיְּימוֹ עוֹד שִׁשָּׁה יָמִים אֲחֵרִים.
which sustains it for an additional six days.
וְזֶהוּ "וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי"
– And this is 'and God blessed the seventh day'—
שֶׁיִּתְרַבֶּה וְיוֹלִיד שִׁשָּׁה יָמִים אֲחֵרִים.
that it multiply and generate another six days.
וְזֶה נִכְתַּב גַּם כֵּן "הַשְּׁבִיעִי" בְּהֵ״א
And this is likewise written HaShevi'i with the definite article Hei
עַל שַׁבַּת דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
alluding to the Sabbath of the Giving of the Torah,
שֶׁיְּקַבְּלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַתּוֹרָה
whereon Israel would accept the Torah
וְיִהְיֶה אֻמָּה שְׁלֵימָה שׁוֹמְרֵי שַׁבָּתוֹת.
and become a unified nation of Sabbath guardians.

h: The Three Dimensions of Shabbat Holiness

p: וְג׳ לְשׁוֹנוֹת אֵלּוּ כְּנֶגֶד ג׳ קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת:
And these three expressions correspond to the three dimensions of Sabbath sanctity: "
וַיְכַל" – כְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין,
Vayechal corresponds to the sanctity of the Field of Holy Apples (Chakal Tapuchin Kadishin / Malchut),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל בֶּאֱמֶת טוֹבִים,
namely that Israel are fundamentally good in truth,
וְנִקְרְאוּ נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל "תַּפּוּחִין"
and the souls of Israel are titled 'apples',
וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל "חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין".
and the Congregation of Israel is the 'Field of Apples'. "
וַיִּשְׁבֹּת מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ"
– Vayishbot mikol melakhto—
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה הַנִּיּוּחָא אַף מֵהֵיפֶךְ הַטּוֹב,
which indicates divine satisfaction even over the opposite of good,
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא,
and this corresponds to the Ancient Holy One (Atika Kadisha / Keter),
שֶׁהוּא מַאֲמַר "בְּרֵאשִׁית",
which is the transcendent utterance Bereishit,
וְעַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת פט:):
and in accordance with what is written (Shabbat 89b): "
אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית – כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ",
'Though your sins be like these solar years that have been prearranged and proceeding since the six days of Creation, they shall become white as snow';
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה
signifying that through repentance motivated by pure love
יְבָרֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁכֵּן הָיָה מְסוּדָּר לְפָנָיו,
Hashem, blessed be He, will reveal that so it was orchestrated before Him,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נְהוֹרָא דְּנָפֵיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא,
so that light should emerge out of darkness,
וּזְדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת כִּזְכִיּוֹת.
and willful sins are converted into merits. "
וַיְבָרֶךְ" – הַבְּרָכָה נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין קַדִּישִׁין,
Vayevarekh—this blessing corresponds to the sanctity of Ze'ir Anpin,
וָא״ו דְּאִקְרֵי אוֹת אֱמֶת (זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּקְרָא),
the letter Vav which is termed the 'sign of truth' (holy Zohar, start of Parashat Vayikra),
וּכְתִיב: "וּשְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד",
and it is written (Proverbs 12:19): 'The lip of truth shall be established forever,'
שֶׁיַּשְׁפִּיעַ הַשָּׂגַת קְדוּשָּׁה וְחַיּוּת לְשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה לְעוֹלָם.
that He channel the apprehension of holiness and vitality into the six workdays perpetually.

h: Three Names of Elohim and the Work of Creation

p: וְכֵן כָּתוּב בַּפָּרָשָׁה ג׳ פְּעָמִים "אֱלֹהִים",
And likewise there is written in the passage three times the Name Elohim,
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם;
which signifies that He is the Master of all forces;
וּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית נִקְרָא "כֹּחַ מַעֲשָׂיו הִגִּיד לְעַמּוֹ", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה.
and the Work of Creation is termed 'the power of His works He declared to His people' (Psalms 111:6), as written in Bereishit Rabbah.
וְלָכֵן בְּמַאֲמַר "וַיְכַל" וּבְמַאֲמַר "וַיְבָרֶךְ" הוּזְכַּר שֵׁם אֱלֹהִים,
Therefore, in the clause Vayechal and in the clause Vayevarekh the Name Elohim is recorded,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁב׳ קְדוּשּׁוֹת אֵלּוּ הֵמָּה מִכֹּחַ אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא
because these two sanctities operate by virtue of the awakening from below (itaruta d'letata)
מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַבְּרִיאָה,
from the side of Israel and Jacob who constitute the ultimate purpose of Creation;
וְעַל זֶה נִכְתַּב שֵׁם אֱלֹהִים שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם,
and regarding this is written the Name Elohim Who is the Master of all powers,
וְאַף הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא הוּא גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and even this awakening from below originates fundamentally from Hashem, blessed be He.
וּבְמַאֲמַר "וַיִּשְׁבֹּת מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ",
However, in the clause 'and He rested from all His work',
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל הַבֵּירוּר "אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ וְכוּלֵי",
which points to the profound rectification of 'though your sins be like these solar years, etc.',
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא,
which corresponds to the sanctity of Atika Kadisha,
לֹא נִכְתַּב שֵׁם אֱלֹהִים,
the Name Elohim is not written,
שֶׁהוּא מִמָּקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ מִזֶּה,
for it stems from a realm far higher than this,
שֶׁהוּא "אַתָּה הוּא עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הָעוֹלָם, אַתָּה הוּא מִשֶּׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם".
the level of 'You were He before the world was created, You are He after the world was created.'
רַק נֶגֶד זֶה נִכְתַּב אַחַר כָּךְ פַּעַם ג׳ שֵׁם אֱלֹהִים:
Only corresponding to this is written subsequently the third occurrence of the Name Elohim: "
כִּי בוֹ שָׁבַת מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים לַעֲשׂוֹת",
'because that in it He rested from all His work which God created to make' (Genesis 2:3),
שֶׁזֶּה מוֹרֶה גַּם כֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִיּוּחָא
which likewise teaches that Hashem, blessed be He, derives divine satisfaction
אַף מִכָּל הַהֵיפֶךְ מֵהַטּוֹב,
even from all that appears opposite to good;

h: Asher Bara Laasot: Man Must Complete the Work

p: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים לַעֲשׂוֹת"
– And this is why it is stated: 'which God created to make'—
שֶׁהָאָדָם יְתַקֵּן,
meaning that man must rectify and complete it,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא, ו):
and as written (Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 11:6):
כָּל מַה שֶּׁנִּבְרָא בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית צְרִיכִין עֲשִׂיָּה,
everything created during the six days of Creation requires further action,
כְּגוֹן הַחַרְדָּל צָרִיךְ לְמָתוֹק וְכוּלֵי,
such as mustard which needs sweetening, etc.,
אֲפִילּוּ אָדָם צָרִיךְ תִּיקּוּן;
even man himself requires spiritual rectification;
וְזֶה נִדְרַשׁ מִדִּכְתִיב "לַעֲשׂוֹת", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב פֵּירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ״י,
and this is derived from the word 'to make' (la'asot), as Rashi explained,
וְכֵן כָּתַב בְּתַנְחוּמָא (פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ ה)
and so is written in Midrash Tanchuma (Parashat Tazria 5)
שֶׁמַּעֲשֵׂה בְּנֵי אָדָם נָאִין לְעִנְיַן הַמִּילָה.
that human craftsmanship is beautiful regarding the mitzvah of circumcision.
וְכֵן מוֹרֶה "לַעֲשׂוֹת" שֶׁהָאָדָם מִצִּדּוֹ יְתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה,
And likewise 'to make' denotes that man from his own initiative must rectify through repentance out of love,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה זְדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת כִּזְכִיּוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יוֹמָא פו.),
so that willful sins are transformed into merits as taught (Yoma 86a),
וְאָז "כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ".
and then 'they shall become white as snow.'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנְחוּמָא (שָׁם פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ):
And as written in Midrash Tanchuma (there): "
אַתָּה עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ רַע וְכוּלֵי,
'You make him evil, etc.,
וְכַמָּה דְּבָרִים קָשִׁים יֵשׁ בָּעוֹלָם יוֹתֵר מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְאַתֶּם מַמְתִּיקִים אוֹתוֹ וְכוּלֵי",
and how many difficult, bitter elements exist in the world far harsher than the evil inclination, yet you sweeten them, etc.,'
וְאָז יִהְיֶה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִיּוּחָא מִכָּל הַהֵיפֶךְ,
and then Hashem, blessed be He, will experience divine satisfaction from all that seemed opposite,
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נַעֲשִׂים כִּזְכִיּוֹת.
when they are converted into actual merits.
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהוּזְכַּר כָּאן "לַעֲשׂוֹת" עַל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם,
And since 'to make' is mentioned here concerning human exertion,
נִזְכַּר כָּאן שֵׁם אֱלֹהִים שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם.
the Name Elohim is recorded here, Who is Master of all faculties.
וְעַל זֶה הוּא אֲרִיכוּת הַגָּלוּת,
And for this purpose is the protracted length of the exile:
שֶׁיְּבוֹרַר כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה מֵאַהֲבָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כִּזְכִיּוֹת,
that all souls of Israel become refined through repentance from love to become merits,
אִישׁ מֵהֶם לֹא נֶעְדָּר.
not a single person among them missing.
אַךְ אִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לֹא יְבָרֵר הָאָדָם מִצִּדּוֹ עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה,
However, if Heaven forbid a person fails to clarify from his own initiative through repentance,
אָז לֶעָתִיד יְבָרֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
then in the ultimate future Hashem, blessed be He, will reveal and clarify: "
וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים",
'And your people are all righteous' (Isaiah 60:21),
וְכָל מַאן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִקְרֵי צַדִּיק,
and whoever is circumcised is designated righteous,
כִּי לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח.
for 'none cast out shall be permanently expelled from Him.'
וְעַל זֶה כְּתִיב מַאֲמַר "וַיִּשְׁבֹּת מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ"
And concerning this is written the clause 'and He rested from all His work',
וְלֹא כְּתִיב בּוֹ שֵׁם אֱלֹהִים,
and the Name Elohim is not written in it—
שֵׁם שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית הַמּוֹרֶה שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל הַכֹּחוֹת כֻּלָּם,
which is the Name of the Work of Creation indicating that He is the Master of all forces—
כֵּיוָן שֶׁקְּדוּשָּׁה זוֹ מֵעַתִּיקָא לְעֵילָּא לְעֵילָּא כָּאָמוּר.
since this transcendent sanctity stems from Atika, exalted on high beyond measure, as stated.

Zohar Chadash, Balak 37-38: “Rabbi Elazar opened and said: “Because you have become precious in My eyes, you have been honored, and I have loved you; I will give a man in your place, and peoples in exchange for your life” (Isaiah 43:4). “Because you have become precious”—it should have said “precious”; it should have said, “Because you are precious in My eyes.” What is meant by “you have become precious”? It implies that he has made himself precious. So it certainly is: any person who is guilty before the Holy One, blessed be He, is at first held in contempt and is an abomination before the Holy One, blessed be He. After he reconsiders and repents of his sin, he has now made himself precious. The Holy One, blessed be He, calls out concerning him and says: “Because you have become precious”—you have made yourself precious.

“In My eyes you have been honored, and I have loved you,” for the Holy One, blessed be He, has love for no person in the world except one who repents of his sin; therefore, “I have loved you.” But what shall I do, since I have given the serpent permission to harm? This is the counsel: “I will give a man in your place.” Who is the “man” whom the Holy One, blessed be He, gives as a ransom in his place? That man who comes from the people of the evil side, so that the serpent may consume what belongs to its own side. For it is written, “I will give a man”—do not read adam, “man,” but Edom. “And peoples”—this is “one people shall be stronger than the other people” (Genesis 25:23). This is the offspring of Esau, given in exchange for his life.”
